column1: # *** "LOS LLERENA DE CANELONES" IN BAUZA - 14 September 2026. *** The jfina tree cited Francisco Bauza,
# "Historia de la Dominacion Espanola en el Uruguay", ed.1929, III p.285, for the Lerenas of Canelones as
# "persona de confianza del Baron de la Laguna en 1817, para vigilar la seguridad y tranquilidad en la
# campana". The book is out of copyright and all three volumes are on archive.org. *** THE PASSAGE WAS READ
# IN FULL, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THE TREE'S SUMMARY SUGGESTS. *** The tree quotes Lecor's own euphemism and
# stops exactly where Bauza's judgement begins. Text below, verbatim, then what it does and does not prove.

column2: Lecor put the resisting Orientals outside the law - "ellos, sus familias y sus propiedades". Portuguese detachments would go out, "*** que quemaran sus haciendas y escoltaran sus familias para a bordo de la escuadra ***". And: "*** Se empleara suficiente numero de personas de confianza, para vigilar por la seguridad y tranquilidad ***, comunicando a los comandantes mas proximos, una relacion circunstanciada de los hechos y del personal de las partidas enemigas, a fin de cumplirse lo mandado"
column3: PRIMARY for the text - *** the published volume read here, archive.org full text ***
column4: *** THIS is the sentence the tree quotes. *** Read whole, "vigilar por la seguridad y tranquilidad" is the occupation's phrase for identifying resisters to men who would then burn their farms and put their families on ships. *** The phrase is a euphemism and the tree reproduces it without the paragraph that follows. ***

column1: *** AND THE PARAGRAPH THAT FOLLOWS NAMES THEM ***
column2: *** Doloroso es manifestar que las mencionadas personas de confianza, fueron los hermanos Alonso de Minas, LOS LLERENA DE CANELONES ***, D. Martin, D. Francisco y D. Bernabe Albin de Colonia, D. Manuel Garcia de Montevideo, un Alanengo de San Jose, un Gandara de Maldonado, y un Rocha que servia de principal baqueano al intruso; *** quienes al frente de grupos cuya totalidad sumaba mas de 400 hombres, se transformaron en azote de los vecindarios de TOLEDO, MANGA y PIEDRAS, haciendo impunemente con ellos, lo que era castigado como un crimen en los patriotas ***
column3: PRIMARY for the text; *** SECONDARY as history - Bauza writing in the 1880s from Pereyra da Silva and a Memoria of the period ***
column4: *** The Llerena of Canelones were not watchmen. They led irregulars for the Portuguese occupation. *** Bauza names eight parties totalling more than 400 men and says they became "the scourge" of three neighbourhoods, doing with impunity what was punished as a crime in patriots. *** "Doloroso es manifestar" - it is painful to state - is his own preface to the list. *** This archive has recorded this family under Oribe in the Guerra Grande; this is thirty years earlier and on the other side of the national story.

column2: Bauza writes "*** LOS LLERENA DE CANELONES ***" - a family, in the plural, with *** NO FORENAMES ***
column4: *** No individual is named, so no person in this register is placed at those events by this text. *** What can be said is narrow and should stay narrow: in 1817 there was a Llerena family at Canelones prominent enough for a national historian to list it among eight collaborating parties - and this archive's Llerena family was at Canelones in exactly that generation, with Sancho aged 50 and his sons Juan Agustin 26, Pedro Antonio 24 and Fidel 17 by the 1812 padron. *** That is a strong identification and it is still an identification. *** It should never be written here as "Sancho did this" or "his sons did this".

column1: *** A NAMESAKE ON THE OTHER SIDE, AND IT IS NOT OURS ***
column2: Same volume: in Rondeau's army, among the ayudantes, "*** D. Jose Pereira Lerena ***"
column4: *** A LERENA serving the patriot army in the same war. *** The compound is PEREIRA LERENA, a different surname pair, and nothing connects him here. *** Recorded so that a future reader who finds "Lerena" in Bauza's index does not attach the wrong man to this family *** - in either direction.

column1: *** TOMES I AND II HOLD NO LERENA AT ALL ***
column2: Both volumes downloaded in full from archive.org and searched for lerena/llerena: *** zero. *** *** CONTROL: *** the word "Montevideo" returns *** 108 *** hits in Tome I and *** 503 *** in Tome II, so the files are real and the search works
